trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.stageNote: The last two entries in the ledger: finish everything the game counts, and the platinum signs the book.
trophies.guide: The platinum. It unlocks on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are in your ledger — there is nothing extra to do for this one beyond completing the whole list. Work the roadmap in order and this is simply the last page.
trophies.tips: If everything else is earned and this has not popped, check the tracker for a trophy you ticked here but did not earn in game — the platinum only counts real unlocks.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.stageNote: The opening chapter. Its two trophies come from simply playing the story; nothing here can be missed.
trophies.guide: Finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission of the game. It is the first thing the story asks of you, so this trophy arrives inside the first hour with no detours needed.
trophies.tips: Use the opening stretch to learn the controls — driving, aiming and the phone — rather than rushing; the later chapters assume all three.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.stageNote: The opening chapter. Its two trophies come from simply playing the story; nothing here can be missed.
trophies.guide: Play through every story mission of Chapter 1 until the chapter closes. Story missions cannot be skipped or failed permanently, so this is a matter of time, not skill.
trophies.tips: Side activities that open during Chapter 1 stay open afterwards; there is no need to clear the map before moving on.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.stageNote: Chapter 2's completion trophy. Keep following the story markers; side content can wait for the cleanup stages.
trophies.guide: Complete every story mission in Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies it is unmissable — the chapter ends when its last mission does, and the trophy follows.
trophies.tips: Bank cash as you go: later trophies ask you to spend and launder large sums, and a healthy balance from the story shortens that grind.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.stageNote: Chapter 3 brings the story to Vice City. Finish the chapter, then let the cleanup stages mop up the city.
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3's story missions. The chapter trophy pops at the chapter break; nothing in the chapter needs a special approach beyond completing its missions.
trophies.tips: Vice City opens a dense cluster of shops, races and collectibles — note their map icons as you pass, but save the sweep for the cleanup stages.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.stageNote: The penultimate chapter. After this, only the finale stands between you and free-roam cleanup.
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4's story missions. Unmissable like the earlier chapter trophies — finish the chapter and the trophy is yours.
trophies.tips: Before the finale, consider a manual save: several missable trophies hang on late-story moments, and a spare save is cheap insurance.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.stageNote: The story's last mission and its gold trophy. Everything after this stage is cleanup at your own pace.
trophies.guide: Complete the game's final story mission. This gold trophy marks the end of the campaign; the world stays open afterwards for the collectibles, activities and 100% cleanup.
trophies.tips: Stock armour and ammunition before starting the finale, and keep the pre-finale save until the credits roll in case a late missable needs a second run.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.stageTitle: Stage 5 — Story missions, as they come
trophies.stageNote: Six named story missions each carry their own trophy. They appear across the chapters; take each one when the story offers it.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Breakfast Run when it appears in your mission list. It is a regular campaign mission, so it cannot be missed — only postponed.
trophies.tips: Mission trophies like this one need no special approach; play the mission normally and the trophy follows the completion screen.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.stageTitle: Stage 5 — Story missions, as they come
trophies.stageNote: Six named story missions each carry their own trophy. They appear across the chapters; take each one when the story offers it.
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist, one of the campaign's set-piece missions. Heists usually allow preparation choices; any route that finishes the mission earns the trophy.
trophies.tips: Bring a full loadout — heist missions are where the game stops holding your hand. Failing a section only restarts a checkpoint, so the trophy itself is never at risk.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.stageTitle: Stage 5 — Story missions, as they come
trophies.stageNote: Six named story missions each carry their own trophy. They appear across the chapters; take each one when the story offers it.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Child's Play. It is part of the main campaign thread, so it will be offered in the normal course of play and cannot be missed.
trophies.tips: Keep the spoiler shield on if you are reading this ledger ahead of your save — mission names alone can hint at story beats.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.stageTitle: Stage 5 — Story missions, as they come
trophies.stageNote: Six named story missions each carry their own trophy. They appear across the chapters; take each one when the story offers it.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. As a campaign mission it is offered automatically and cannot be missed; finish it and the trophy is recorded.
trophies.tips: If a mission gives you a choice of approach, pick the one matching your loadout — the trophy only cares that the mission ends, not how.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.stageTitle: Stage 5 — Story missions, as they come
trophies.stageNote: Six named story missions each carry their own trophy. They appear across the chapters; take each one when the story offers it.
trophies.guide: Finish VCIA Takedown, the story mission set around Vice City's airport authority. It is a normal campaign mission, so the trophy is unmissable — but keep an eye out during it for the related missable departure trophy (Catch Me If You Can).
trophies.tips: Save before starting this mission: the airport sequence also holds a one-time moment another trophy depends on, and a spare save costs nothing.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.stageTitle: Stage 5 — Story missions, as they come
trophies.stageNote: Six named story missions each carry their own trophy. They appear across the chapters; take each one when the story offers it.
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory. Another named campaign mission with its own trophy; play it when the story offers it and the trophy follows.
trophies.tips: Operations with codenames tend to be combat-heavy — top up armour and special ammunition before you accept the mission marker.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.stageNote: The last two entries in the ledger: finish everything the game counts, and the platinum signs the book.
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion on the game's own checklist — story, strangers, collectibles, activities and everything else the completion counter tracks. This gold trophy is the long tail of the platinum: most of its hours are the same cleanup the other trophies already ask for, so work it last with the in-game checklist open.
trophies.tips: Use the game's completion screen as the source of truth and tick categories off in this ledger as they close; the final few percent are usually one forgotten activity type.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts — the count comes straight from the official description. Stunts are the game's marked jumps and stunt challenges scattered across Leonida; each one you land cleanly adds to the tracked total.
trophies.tips: Do these in a fast, forgiving vehicle and in daylight; a stunt that ends in a crash usually does not count, so clean landings beat speed.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity the game offers at least once — races, shooting range, fishing, arcade, drone races, bowling and the rest of the activity menu. You do not need to win any of them for this trophy; one honest attempt at each type is enough.
trophies.tips: Open the activity list on the map and work down it; this trophy is also a good way to discover which activities you enjoy before their harder trophies.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — PlayStation tracks 42 of them. Each challenge is a timed accuracy course; gold means beating its top score threshold, so expect to replay the harder courses until the patterns stick.
trophies.tips: Learn one course at a time and chase accuracy before speed: most gold thresholds punish missed targets more than slow ones. Save between courses so a bad run never costs progress.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location — there are 14 of them. Each location runs its own course against the clock or rival drones; you need a first-place finish at each, not just participation.
trophies.tips: Drone handling rewards smooth lines over aggression: brake early for gates, and replay a course once to learn it before racing it for the win.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word that matters is 'different': winning the same street race twenty times does not count, so spread your wins across the race locations on the map.
trophies.tips: Bring an upgraded car in the right class for each event, and tick races off in this ledger as you win them so you do not repeat one by mistake.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.missableWhy: The opponent is a named character, Cal. Character challenges belong to that character's strand of missions, and strands close as the story moves on — once Cal's story is done, the challenge may no longer be offered.
trophies.missableWindow: While Cal's missions and challenges are still available
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal head-to-head in a fishing challenge. Find Cal's fishing challenge when it is offered, out-fish him over the challenge's time limit, and the trophy is yours. Because the challenge belongs to a named character, take it while Cal is still around rather than leaving it for the very end.
trophies.tips: Fishing challenges are usually won on patience: cast, wait for the bite indicator, and reel steadily instead of yanking. Lose once and you can retry while the challenge remains open.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Complete any one arcade game — play a cabinet game through to its end screen. It does not need to be a high score or a full clear of every level; finishing a single game is enough.
trophies.tips: Arcade cabinets sit in bars and arcades around the map; pick the shortest game you can find if you only want the trophy.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.stageNote: The named side characters each end with a final mission. Their strands can be played during or after the main story.
trophies.guide: Work through Andy's mission strand to its final mission and complete it. Side strands unlock one mission at a time, often with a wait between them, so start Andy's early and check back as new markers appear.
trophies.tips: If Andy's next marker has not appeared, advance the clock by sleeping or doing another activity — strand missions often unlock after in-game time passes.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.stageNote: The named side characters each end with a final mission. Their strands can be played during or after the main story.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission — the last entry in his strand of side missions. Play each of Kenton's missions as they unlock until the strand closes with its finale.
trophies.tips: Strand finales are usually longer than the missions before them; arrive with armour and a full magazine.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.stageNote: The named side characters each end with a final mission. Their strands can be played during or after the main story.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission strand by completing its final mission. As with the other named characters, the strand opens gradually — take each mission as it appears and the finale will follow.
trophies.tips: Keep a note of which strands you have started; with several running at once it is easy to lose track of who still owes you a finale.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.stageNote: The named side characters each end with a final mission. Their strands can be played during or after the main story.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full mission strands for strangers across Leonida — whole storylines, not single missions. The named strands in this stage (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) count toward the eight, so finishing those finales moves this silver trophy most of the way.
trophies.tips: Stranger markers appear as you explore; whenever a new one pops up, start it the same session so its later missions unlock while you clean up other trophies.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.stageNote: The named side characters each end with a final mission. Their strands can be played during or after the main story.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Randy's strand. Play Randy's missions as they unlock; the strand's last mission carries this trophy.
trophies.tips: If a strand seems stalled, check your phone and map after sleeping — follow-up missions often arrive by message.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.stageNote: The named side characters each end with a final mission. Their strands can be played during or after the main story.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's strand by completing its final mission. The strand unlocks step by step like the others; the trophy pops when the last mission ends.
trophies.tips: Five named finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) plus three more stranger strands make the eight that Strangers & Freaks asks for — plan them together.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida — 18 spots in total. Each spot is a marked place where the meditate prompt appears; sit at all of them once and the trophy is yours.
trophies.tips: Sweep region by region with a helicopter or fast car, and tick spots off as you go — the last one is always the one you drove past twice.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.missableWhy: The hunt is a favour for a named character, Bret, and the animal is described as unique — a one-off target tied to his strand. Once Bret's strand closes, there may be no way to ask for the hunt again.
trophies.stageNote: The named side characters each end with a final mission. Their strands can be played during or after the main story.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Accept Bret's hunting request when his strand offers it, track the named animal, and bring it down — a unique target means one animal, one chance per attempt, so do it while Bret's missions are open.
trophies.tips: Use a scoped rifle and approach downwind and crouched; unique animals tend to flee at the first loud noise, and a missed shot can mean a long re-track.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full Collectible Card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida and grouped into themed sets; finishing any three complete sets earns this silver trophy — you do not need every card in the game.
trophies.tips: Pick the three smallest sets first and hunt them region by region. Cards often sit on rooftops, piers and other places you only reach on foot, so park and walk the last stretch.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It action at 100 different locations — the count is in the official description. WAiNK spots are marked points of interest around the state; trigger the action at each one and the tracked counter climbs to 100.
trophies.tips: Combine this with the meditation spots and area exploration: one slow drive around Leonida can tick three collectible trophies at once.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Complete 50 Challenges from the game's challenge list — the short tracked tasks (driving, combat, exploration and the like) shown in the pause menu. Any 50 count; pick the ones that fit how you already play.
trophies.tips: Skim the challenge list early and let the passive ones (distance driven, vehicles used) complete themselves during the story, then mop up the rest in cleanup.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missableWhy: It needs your partner beside you while wanted. The partner rides with you during specific stretches of the story; once the campaign ends, that window may close for good.
trophies.missableWindow: While your partner is travelling with you in the story
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: With your partner in the car, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose it and escape the heat together. Do this while the story still has your partner riding with you — the official description makes the partner part of the requirement, so a solo escape does not count.
trophies.tips: Pick a fast car with good armour, raise the stars away from the city centre, then break line of sight in tunnels or underpasses and stay hidden until the stars clear.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missableWhy: Like Hot Together, it requires your partner present for the whole spree. Partner availability is a story window, not a permanent free-roam feature.
trophies.missableWindow: While your partner is travelling with you in the story
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner alongside, keeping your wanted level the whole time — if the stars clear between shops, the chain breaks. Choose three shops close together, rob each register, and drive straight to the next without hiding.
trophies.tips: Scout the trio first: short hops between doors keep the heat alive. Keep the engine running and the car pointed at the next shop before you go in.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — get into (or otherwise register) 100 distinct vehicle models across Leonida. Everyday traffic covers most of the count; the last few are the rare ones parked at docks, airfields and dealerships.
trophies.tips: Swap cars often while travelling instead of keeping one favourite, and check vehicle showrooms and marinas for models that never appear in traffic.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Take down five enemies during one single use of Combat Focus, the game's slow-motion aiming ability. You need five hostiles alive and in range when you trigger it, so set it up in a gang hideout or a busy robbery rather than hoping a random fight cooperates.
trophies.tips: Group the enemies first: let them bunch up at a doorway, then trigger Combat Focus and work headshots across the group before the meter drains.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableWhy: VCIA is the airport authority from the story mission VCIA Takedown. An 'unscheduled departure' is a specific moment inside that mission's sequence — once the mission is over, the moment is gone.
trophies.missableWindow: During the VCIA Takedown story mission
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — in plain terms, leave the airport in a way nobody scheduled: take an aircraft (or another vehicle) out of VCIA during the airport sequence instead of following the planned exit. It belongs to the VCIA Takedown mission window, so grab it while you are there.
trophies.tips: Save before VCIA Takedown. If the mission ends and this has not popped, reload and look for the aircraft the objective does not point at.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.missableWhy: Rhinos are military tanks; they appear in specific story set-pieces rather than free-roam traffic. If the tank sequence belongs to one mission, the chance to deal with one ends with it.
trophies.missableWindow: During the story sequence that fields Rhino tanks
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Deal with a Rhino tank — the description ('Kinda hot in these Rhinos') points at getting inside one and feeling the heat, most plausibly stealing or commandeering a Rhino during the military set-piece that fields them. When tanks appear in the story, make one yours instead of just surviving them.
trophies.tips: Tanks shrug off small arms. Approach on foot from behind during the chaos, and save before the sequence so a failed grab costs a reload, not the trophy.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — no alarms tripped, no witnesses raising the heat, no wanted level during the job. Case the store first, move when staff and cameras are looking elsewhere, and leave quietly with the take.
trophies.tips: Night visits are quieter. If a wanted level appears, the attempt is void — walk away, let things cool, and try the same store again another day.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape after each one — the count and the escape both matter. Bank jobs are the heaviest free-roam robberies: plan an exit vehicle, expect a high wanted level, and make sure you actually get away before counting the vault.
trophies.tips: Stage a fast, armoured car outside before you go in, and scout each bank's rear exit. Losing the heat in a tunnel or underpass beats outrunning it on the highway.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape with the take. Armored trucks run set routes through the city; block one, deal with the guards, grab the cash from the back, and lose the wanted level that follows.
trophies.tips: A heavy vehicle makes the best roadblock. Hit the truck away from police stations and have your escape route picked before the first shot.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — visit every one of the state's 52 areas so the whole map is uncovered. Flying the coastline and the highways in a grid clears most areas quickly; the last few are the small neighbourhoods you never had a reason to enter.
trophies.tips: Pair this with the meditation spots and WAiNK locations: one slow tour of the state feeds three trophies at once.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each gang — Leonida has 9 gangs, and each runs its own operations. You need one successful robbery per gang, not every operation on the map, so pick the softest target each gang owns.
trophies.tips: Operations are defended; scout from a distance, note the guard count, and hit the cash point fast rather than clearing the whole site.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.missableWhy: The name says it: 'In The Beginning…' points at an early-game moment, and Ocean Beach is where the story opens. Early set-pieces tied to the opening chapters often cannot be revisited once the story moves inland.
trophies.missableWindow: Early game, while the story is still around Ocean Beach
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Find the beachfront bar spot overlooking the water early in the game, order the cocktail, and take in the view — a small, quiet moment the ledger flags as early-game, so do not leave Ocean Beach without it.
trophies.tips: Do this during your first hours in the game, before the story pulls you inland; it takes a minute and removes all doubt about the window.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missableWhy: Smashing out of a showroom 'in classic style' reads like a scripted story set-piece — a specific showroom, a specific car, a specific window. Set-pieces belong to their mission and do not repeat in free roam.
trophies.missableWindow: During the story sequence set in the vehicle showroom
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style: when the story puts you inside a showroom with a car, drive it out through the glass instead of using the door. The trophy is about the exit, not the theft — make the departure loud and through the window.
trophies.tips: Save before any mission that starts inside a dealership. If the mission ends without the trophy, reload and aim for the glass, not the ramp.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.stageNote: The cleanup sweep: counts, sets and challenges. Nothing here closes, so take it in any order after the story.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley and follow through — complete a game there. The trophy names one specific alley, so other lanes do not count; head to Kolt & Associates and finish a full game.
trophies.tips: You do not need a good score, just a finished game. It also counts toward trying every activity type for Master of None.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.missableWhy: The description describes a partnership moment — a specific beat between the two leads. Story beats happen once; if the moment is a choice or a scene outcome, it cannot be replayed on the same save.
trophies.missableWindow: During the story, at the partnership beat it describes
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal — the official description is deliberately vague, but it points at a specific moment between you and your partner that lands with an audience. Play the partnership scenes attentively rather than skipping them, and keep a save from before major partner missions so the beat can be revisited if it passes quietly.
trophies.tips: Because the description hides the trigger, the safe play is simple: never skip partner cutscenes, and keep rotating saves through the middle chapters.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Make choices — PlayStation tracks a count of choices made, running to 500. Dialogue picks, mission approaches and everyday decisions all feed the counter, so this trophy fills up simply by playing the story and engaging with its decision points instead of skipping them.
trophies.tips: Answer calls, pick dialogue options and choose approaches in missions; the counter rewards participation, not any particular choice.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missableWhy: 'Second time's the charm' implies a specific attempt that can fail once and succeed on the retry — a scripted moment with a built-in first failure. Scripted moments happen once per save.
trophies.missableWindow: At the story moment the description hints at; keep a save before it
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Succeed on a second try. The description suggests a moment designed to go wrong the first time — when something fails in a way that feels scripted rather than accidental, take the retry the game offers instead of reloading an older save, and the trophy should follow the successful second attempt.
trophies.tips: Resist the reflex to reload after a suspicious failure. If the game itself offers the second attempt, that offer is probably the trophy's doorway.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.missableWhy: 'What the hell just happened?' is the reaction to a one-off strange event. Scripted weirdness happens at a fixed point in the story and does not repeat in free roam.
trophies.missableWindow: At the story's strange-event moment; do not skip the scene
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Witness something strange. Somewhere in the story there is a moment that earns that reaction — a bizarre event, sighting or encounter. Play the campaign without skipping scenes and stay in the moment when the game gets weird; the trophy is for being there when it happens.
trophies.tips: Explore odd map markers and stranger encounters as they appear rather than mainlining the story; strange events like to hide one step off the main path.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Bowl someone over with a melee drive-by: from a moving vehicle, lean out and knock a pedestrian down with a melee weapon. Ride slowly past a target on a quiet street, swing as you pass, and the trophy counts the knockdown.
trophies.tips: A motorcycle or an open-top car gives the cleanest swing. One clean hit is enough — this is a single knockdown, not a spree.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Robberies and heists pay in marked bills that cannot be spent directly; run them through your laundering contacts until the lifetime laundered total reaches a quarter of a million.
trophies.tips: Feed the launderer steadily after every big score instead of hoarding marked bills — the trophy counts money earned through laundering, so regular small washes beat one late dump.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — clothes, weapons, vehicle upgrades, food, anything bought over a counter counts toward the lifetime total. By the cleanup stages you will likely be most of the way there from normal play; a few vehicle upgrades finish the job.
trophies.tips: Buy the expensive upgrades you were going to buy anyway (armour, vehicle mods) rather than dumping cash on clothes at the end.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties around Leonida. Garages are buyable properties that store your vehicles; the trophy needs every one of them owned, so save the story's earnings and buy them up during cleanup.
trophies.tips: Property prices vary by neighbourhood; buy the cheap rural garages first and let robbery income fund the Vice City ones.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.stageNote: The free-roam mischief: robberies, wanted levels, money and property. Most of it waits until after the story — the partner trophies do not.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app tracks vehicles you own or store; add ten different vehicles to it — bought, stored in your garages, or otherwise registered — and the trophy completes.
trophies.tips: This pairs naturally with buying the garage properties: fill each new garage with a different vehicle and register them as you go.
